newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Barings sees 15 pct Brazil devaluation early '99.
newsitem.headline: Barings sees 15 pct Brazil devaluation early '99.

text.p: Brazil will face a devaluation of 15 percent in the real currency early in 1999 after next year's presidential elections, ING Barings said Thursday in a seminar in Argentina.

"We are worried about Brazil. If it posts annual growth of more than three percent, its balance of payments will unravel and problems will appear," said Arturo Porzecanski, chief economist for ING Barings in the Americas.

"They will not carry out a devaluation before the 1998 presidential vote, but that (three percent) limit may be broken, which is why we expect a devaluation of the real in 1999," he said at a meeting at the Buenos Aires bolsa.
According to Porzecanski, the devaluation would help Brazil gain a competitive edge by improving its trade balance, quite apart from the policy of mini-devaluations it is currently applying.
"The aim of the devaluation is to promote exports and reduce imports," he said, stressing such a move would hurt the level of Argentine exports.
